tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks: public bench script and src/ programs, Scheme compiler versions and flags stated, CPU Intel i3-N305 stated in the repo's index.html), but Bigloo compiles through the Arch gcc whose version is not stated anywhere, so it falls just short of A.

corrections.hardware: Intel Core i3-N305 @ 3.8 GHz, 48 GB RAM, Arch Linux packages (per the suite's index.html); results logs show host kernel Linux 6.16.8-arch3-1 x86_64; Bigloo and Guile runs dated 2026-01-16.
corrections.license: GPL-2.0-or-later (compiler and tools) AND LGPL-2.0-or-later (run-time system and libraries, 'GNU Library General Public License' per the repo LICENSE file)
corrections.compiler_and_flags: bench script: bigloo '<file> -O6 -call/cc -copt -O3 -o <out>' (C backend; the C compiler is the Arch Linux gcc, version not stated); Guile 'guild compile -O3' with GC_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE=100000000; Chez '--optimize-level 2 --program'; versions bigloo-4.6a, guile-3.0.11, chez-10.3.0+r7rs; one run per benchmark (NB_RUNS=1), times are the in-program elapsed time printed per benchmark.
corrections.caveats: Independent community suite run on an Intel Core i3-N305 (low-power 8-core Alder Lake-N) with Arch packages; the page says 'No guarantees for any of the numbers', each benchmark is run once, and the gcc version behind Bigloo's C backend is not stated, so tier B. Bigloo has failed or crashed rows in all.csv (ctak ULIMITKILLED, mbrotZ COMPILEERROR, pi CRASHED, compiler COMPILEERROR, slatex CRASHED, chudnovsky CRASHED, equal ULIMITKILLED) which are excluded from the derived geomean. Bigloo's repo has a bench/ directory (bague, earley, fft, maze, etc.) but no committed comparison with Guile or Chez was found. Chez Scheme (already listed) beats Bigloo on aggregate (about 0.63x derived, Bigloo faster on 18 of 50 shared rows), and Bigloo loses to Guile on 14 of 50 shared rows (deriv, destruc, diviter, divrec, puzzle, cpstak, fibc, ack, string, earley, graphs, matrix, nboyer, gcbench). Lua not part of the suite. Bigloo 4.6a in the suite is not necessarily the repo head.

notes: All quoted numbers and the derived ratios re-computed from all.csv (36 of 50 faster than Guile, geomean 1.615x; versus Chez 0.629x). Shortcomings: slower than already-listed Chez on aggregate, slower than Guile on 14 of 50 rows, seven failed/crashed rows, single run on a low-power i3-N305, backend gcc version unstated. The repo LICENSE splits licences: compiler GPL-2.0-or-later, runtime and libraries GNU Library GPL.

tier_reason: Well-known independent suite (ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks: public bench script and src/ programs, gambitc-v4.9.7 'gsc -o <out> -exe', CPU Intel i3-N305 stated in the repo's index.html), but gsc compiles through gcc (named only in an error line of results.GambitC) with the Arch package's default C flags and no stated gcc version, so it falls just short of A.

corrections.hardware: Intel Core i3-N305 @ 3.8 GHz, 48 GB RAM, Arch Linux packages (per the suite's index.html); results logs show host kernel Linux 6.16.8-arch3-1 x86_64; Gambit run dated 2026-02-03 (re-run after the commit 'Run with correct gambit-c version', same host and kernel), Guile run 2026-01-16.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: bench script: Gambit 'gsc -o <out> -exe <file>' with no extra flags (safe mode, no 'declare (not safe)'); the C compiler is gcc (named in results.GambitC; version and the packaged gsc default C flags not stated); Guile 'guild compile -O3' then run with GC_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE=100000000; Chez '--optimize-level 2 --program'; versions in all.csv gambitc-v4.9.7, guile-3.0.11, chez-10.3.0+r7rs; one run per benchmark (NB_RUNS=1). Packages are the Arch Linux packages per README.
corrections.caveats: Independent community suite run on an Intel Core i3-N305 with Arch packages; the page says 'No guarantees for any of the numbers', each benchmark runs once, and the gcc version and default C flags behind gsc are not stated, so tier B not A. Gambit was re-run on 2026-02-03 while Guile and Chez ran on 2026-01-16 (same host and kernel). The 1.95x geomean is a derived figure over rows matched by exact benchmark name; floating-point rows named with '35.' versus '35.0' in different implementations were not paired. Gambit's own bench/ directory commits no comparison results, and the Gambit repo makes no benchmark claim. Chez Scheme (already listed) beats Gambit on aggregate (geomean about 0.79 derived), and Gambit is slower than Guile on 8 of 53 rows (pi, string, dynamic, graphs, paraffins, chudnovsky, nboyer, gcbench), much slower on string and bignum rows. Lua was not part of the suite, so no Lua comparison is recorded. Gambit has one COMPILEERROR row ('compiler': gcc's cc1 was killed while compiling the generated C) in all.csv, excluded from the geomean.

notes: All quoted numbers and derived ratios re-computed from all.csv (45 of 53 faster than Guile, geomean 1.953x; versus Chez 0.794x, faster on 17 of 54). Shortcomings: slower than already-listed Chez on aggregate, slower than Guile on 8 rows (string 15.6x slower, pi 7.1x, gcbench 5.6x), single run on a low-power i3-N305, gcc version unstated. Licence kept as Apache-2.0 OR LGPL-2.1: the repo root ships LICENSE-2.0.txt and LGPL.txt (v2.1) and GitHub shows both, but no README text states the dual-licence terms and source headers say 'All Rights Reserved'.

tier_reason: Upgraded from B: ecraven/r7rs-benchmarks publishes the bench script (loko_comp: 'loko -std=r7rs -ftarget=linux --compile', guile_comp: 'guild compile -O3') and the src/ programs, all.csv names loko-0.12.1 and guile-3.0.11, and the repo's index.html states the CPU (Intel Core i3-N305 @ 3.8 GHz); Loko emits machine code itself with no C toolchain, so code, compiler, flags and CPU model are all stated.

corrections.hardware: Intel Core i3-N305 @ 3.8 GHz, 48 GB RAM, Arch Linux packages (per the suite's index.html); results logs show host kernel Linux 6.16.8-arch3-1 x86_64; Loko and Guile runs dated 2026-01-16.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: bench script: 'loko -std=r7rs -ftarget=linux --compile <file> --output <out>' (native code, no C compiler involved); Guile 'guild compile -O3' with GC_INITIAL_HEAP_SIZE=100000000; Chez '--optimize-level 2 --program'; versions loko-0.12.1, guile-3.0.11, chez-10.3.0+r7rs; one run per benchmark (NB_RUNS=1).
corrections.claimed_speedup: From all.csv (derived from page data): loko-0.12.1 is faster than guile-3.0.11 on 48 of 51 shared benchmarks with numeric results, geomean about 1.62x (about 1.52x over 45 rows when the floating-point rows fft, mbrot, mbrotZ, pnpoly, ray and simplex are left out). Examples: tak:40:20:11:1 1.6679999828338623 s vs 3.113433651 s; fib:40:5 3.927000045776367 vs 6.489886582; ctak:32:16:8:1 19.98699951171875 vs 83.031008426; mbrot:75:1000 6.51200008392334 vs 22.496891153; cat:50 3.4140000343322754 vs 15.986089402; paraffins:23:10 1.7589999437332153 vs 3.866057371. Slower: string:500000:100 5.241000175476074 vs 0.204681098; pi:50:500:50:100 156.49200439453125 vs 0.107659156; chudnovsky:50:500:50:1000 also slower. Versus chez-10.3.0+r7rs geomean about 0.65x (Loko faster in 22 of 52). Loko's README adds an own startup claim: REPL starts in 1.2 ms +/- 0.2 ms on an AMD 3950X per hyperfine (no baseline named) and 'does fairly well in the R7RS benchmarks'.
corrections.caveats: Independent community suite run once per benchmark on an Intel Core i3-N305 with Arch packages; the page says 'No guarantees for any of the numbers'. Loko has INCORRECT results on three floating-point rows (sumfp returned 4.99873677312e11, nucleic 33.797950744628906, sum1 15794.6416015625, all consistent with single-precision flonum arithmetic) and an out-of-heap-memory crash on earley, all excluded from the geomean; the float rows that passed (fft, mbrot, pnpoly, ray, simplex) may also have run at reduced precision and flatter Loko, and without those float rows the derived geomean drops to about 1.52x. Pathological on bignum arithmetic: pi:50:500:50:100 takes 156.5 s versus 0.108 s for Guile. Chez Scheme (already listed) beats Loko on aggregate (about 0.65x derived). The loko 0.12.1 result in all.csv may not match the current head. Lua not part of the suite.

notes: All quoted numbers re-computed from all.csv (48 of 51 faster than Guile, geomean 1.617x; versus Chez 0.648x, faster on 22 of 52); the third slower row (chudnovsky) was missing from the record. Upgraded to A because the CPU model is on the suite's index.html and Loko needs no C compiler; shortcomings: three INCORRECT float rows that look like single-precision flonums (possible flattering of passing float rows), earley out of heap, catastrophic bignum pi row, slower than already-listed Chez, single run. GitLab API confirms EUPL-1.2, 64 stars, not a fork, last commit 2026-10-03.
